p1: [low, ominous] In nineteen nineteen, a serial killer wrote to a newspaper... [whispers] and promised to spare every home playing jazz.
[low] New Orleans, nineteen eighteen. [low, tense] Someone was breaking into homes at night.
[low] He chiselled through the door... [whispers] and let himself in.
[low, ominous] Then he used the family's own axe.
[low, ominous] At least six people were killed.
[low] Then, in March nineteen nineteen, the Times-Picayune printed a letter.
[low] The writer called himself... [whispers] a demon from the hottest hell.
[low, ominous] He named the night: Tuesday... at twelve fifteen.
[low] And one promise: [whispers] any home with a jazz band playing... would be spared.
[low, tense] That night, the whole city played jazz. Bars and cafés were packed.
[whispers] And that night... nobody was killed.
[low, ominous] But it didn't stop him. He struck again that same year.
[low] To this day, nobody knows if that letter was really his... [whispers] or who he was.
[low, ominous] He was never caught. [whispers] Just like the letter said.
